subject: Media Literacy
title: Mass Surveillance Programs
description: A 60-second lesson on Mass Surveillance Programs.

hook.text: In 2013, Edward Snowden revealed the NSA was collecting phone records of millions of Americans. The world was stunned.

buildup.text: Governments conduct mass surveillance — monitoring communications of entire populations, not just suspects.

discovery.text: Programs like PRISM collected data directly from tech companies. XKeyscore searched virtually all internet activity.

twist.text: These programs were secret and operated with minimal oversight. Courts later ruled some were illegal.

climax.text: Mass surveillance treats every citizen as a potential suspect. The presumption of innocence is reversed by design.

punchline.text: They weren't watching suspects. They were watching everyone, looking for suspects.

quiz.question: What did the Snowden revelations expose?
options: Government mass surveillance programs collecting data on millions of ordinary citizens
Social media manipulation by foreign governments
